small_guidance:
- Add larger GEMM autotune configs (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) and a GROUP_M=8 swizzle for L2 reuse — M=N=2048-8192 with K=8192 benefits from bigger tiles.
- Pre-transpose W once (or load W with K on the inner contiguous axis) so the K-loop avoids `tl.trans` on each iteration; W is [N,K] with stride_wk=1, so loading as [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] directly removes the transpose.
- Drop the scalar logsumexp/mean/gelu kernel and fuse it: since the post-GEMM tensor is reduced to a single scalar per row then broadcast-added to original_x, you can skip materializing Y entirely — accumulate the row-sum of (X@W^T + b - sub) inside the GEMM epilogue (atomic-add into a per-row sum buffer across N tiles), then a tiny kernel does /N + GELU + residual add.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a single split-K reduction kernel: the only thing that leaves the GEMM is `sum_n(W[n,:] @ x[m,:] + b[n] - sub[n])` per row m. Compute partial row sums with one program per (M tile, N tile) using `tl.dot` and atomic-add into `row_sum[M]`; this avoids writing the full [M,N]=2048x8192 Y tensor (64 MB) and its re-read.
- Then a single fused epilogue kernel reads row_sum, divides by N, applies GELU (logsumexp of size-1 is identity), and adds to original_x in one pass — one read of x, one write of out, no intermediate [M,N] traffic.
- Alternatively, since each output row needs only one scalar, structure as persistent per-row programs that loop over N in BLOCK_N chunks, each doing a [1,K] x [K,BLOCK_N] dot — but the split-K + atomic approach keeps `tl.dot` tiles square and is likely faster on 4090.
